sources.label: WeBWorK Open Problem Library
sources.license_note: Generally CC BY-NC-SA unless otherwise indicated; verify per source record when possible.
sources.notes: Strong default source for mathematics problem retrieval.

sources.label: OpenStax
sources.license_note: Books may be CC BY or CC BY-NC-SA; verify the specific book license.
sources.notes: Good source for textbook-style exercises and review items.

sources.label: MIT OpenCourseWare
sources.license_note: Open course materials with Creative Commons licensing; confirm page-level terms when needed.
sources.notes: Useful for assignments, exams, proof prompts, and richer content extracts.

sources.label: LibreTexts
sources.license_note: Licensing varies by page and book; always review before ingestion.
sources.notes: Good source, but license checks must stay page-specific.

sources.label: Project Euler
sources.license_note: Main problem archive is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
sources.notes: Best for enrichment and challenge problems.

sources.label: CS Unplugged
sources.license_note: Activities are open source under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike.
sources.notes: Good source for concept-focused computer science activities.

sources.label: Paul's Online Math Notes
sources.license_note: Free online notes and downloadable PDFs are publicly available; keep attribution and use review-first until reuse terms are confirmed per page.
sources.notes: Good web-first source for calculus explanations, worked examples, and module content support.

sources.label: User-Provided Document
sources.license_note: Use only within the current course workflow and review provenance manually.
sources.notes: Preferred source type when the user directly provides a PDF or other course document.
